comments.text:
Interesting to see bigger 1% low drops only in 1080p. The PUBG results in 1080p probably aren't really the GPU. At 1080p it isn't entirely the GPU bottleneck now is it? The CPU can still cause that stutter at those high frame rates. (You've done your best on CPU choice sure but these things happen right?) So you're right not to call it representative. Pure numbers though, putting up bar graphs of the same game but at different resolutions might not be the best way, specifically because of this difference in where the bottleneck shifts - the one thing I was interested in and was doing mental math for was the percentage drop between the AVG and the 1% low, also to catch the pattern when it is definitely more GPU-constrained.

And you've got a nice beefy card with a good-looking cooling solution, have you tried checking what you can achieve with overclocking? I've got a feeling it could be representative of an average user of a higher-end GPU to at least try Auto-OC with Afterburner or some other "quick and easy OC" attempt. It seems like you don't test for noise levels (I don't know the limitations to your equipment there) but it would be a good way to really challenge your ears to see if with an aggressive fan curve and auto-OC if it's worth it in that direction to squeeze more FPS out for a little more noise and heat, to further qualify those limits better.
